ai.literal: Out of love they desire not, wealth who desire, women with choice bracelets, sweet words ruin will bring.
ai.translation: The sweet words of women with choice bracelets, who desire wealth and not out of genuine love, will bring ruin.
ai.modern: அன்பினால் விரும்பாமல் பொருளை மட்டுமே விரும்பும் அழகிய வளையல்களை அணிந்த பெண்களின் இனிய சொற்கள் ஒருவனுக்குத் துன்பத்தைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the deceptive sweetness of courtesans. It describes them as women wearing exquisite bracelets who show affection not out of genuine love, but out of a desire for wealth. Their sweet words are not expressions of true feeling but tools for financial gain. Believing and yielding to such false sweetness will ultimately bring a person to ruin and disgrace.

ai.literal: Profit having-weighed affection who-speak character-without women's motive having-weighed without-associating abandon.
ai.translation: Weigh the true motives of characterless women who speak words of affection only after weighing their profit, and abandon them without associating with them.
ai.modern: தமக்குக் கிடைக்கும் பொருளைக் கணக்கிட்டு அன்பாகப் பேசும் பண்பில்லாத பெண்களின் உண்மையான நோக்கத்தை ஆராய்ந்து, அவர்களோடு உறவு கொள்ளாமல் விட்டுவிட வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against women who feign affection purely for financial gain. The word 'பயன்' (profit) reveals their primary motivation, while 'பண்பு' (affection or good quality) is what they falsely project to their suitors. The poet uses a clever contrast between the 'பண்பு' they speak and their actual state of being 'பண்பின்' (without character). By weighing ('தூக்கி') their true motives just as carefully as they weigh their profit, one should avoid their company entirely.

ai.literal: wealth women falseness embrace darkness room-in stranger corpse having-embraced like-that
ai.translation: The false embrace of women who desire only wealth is like hugging a stranger's corpse in a dark room.
ai.modern: பொருளுக்காக ஆசைப்படும் பெண்களின் பொய்யான தழுவல், ஓர் இருட்டு அறையில் முன்பின் தெரியாத ஒரு பிணத்தைக் கட்டிப்பிடிப்பதற்குச் சமமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet vividly describes the loveless nature of women who offer intimacy solely for money. Their embrace is termed 'false' because it lacks genuine affection and warmth. The poet compares this act to hugging an unknown corpse in a pitch-black room. The darkness signifies the blindness of lust, while the stranger's corpse highlights the utter lack of life, feeling, and true connection in such an embrace.

ai.literal: Wealth as their goal those who have, their base charm will not embrace, grace as wealth seeking those of wisdom.
ai.translation: The wise who seek the higher wealth of grace will not embrace the base charms of women who care only for material wealth.
ai.modern: அருளாகிய செல்வத்தை நாடும் அறிஞர்கள், பணத்தையே குறியாகக் கொண்ட விலைமகளிரின் அற்பமான இன்பத்தைத் தீண்ட மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts two types of wealth: material money and spiritual grace. Women who sell their affection care only for material wealth, offering a base and meaningless physical charm in return. Men of true wisdom, who seek the higher wealth of grace and compassion, recognize this emptiness and will never touch such superficial pleasures.

ai.literal: Women of public charm's / base charm / they will not embrace / by goodness of mind / glorious / those of wisdom.
ai.translation: Those whose wisdom is made glorious by the goodness of their mind will not embrace the base charms of women who offer their charms to all.
ai.modern: சிறந்த அறிவும் நல்ல மனமும் உடையவர்கள், பொருள் கொடுப்பவர் அனைவருக்கும் பொதுவான இன்பம் தரும் மகளிரின் அற்பமான இன்பத்தை நாட மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: The couplet contrasts two kinds of 'goodness' or 'charm' (நலம்). The women offer a 'public charm' (பொதுநலம்) which the poet calls a 'base charm' (புன்னலம்). In contrast, the wise possess the 'goodness of mind' (மதிநலம்) which makes their wisdom glorious. Because their minds are elevated, they will not degrade themselves by seeking the cheap, transactional affection of prostitutes.

ai.literal: Own goodness those who protect will not embrace, beauty being proud, base pleasure those who offer's shoulders.
ai.translation: Those who cultivate their own virtue will not embrace the shoulders of women who, proud of their charms, offer base pleasures.
ai.modern: தமது நல்லொழுக்கத்தைப் போற்றிக் காப்பவர்கள், தமது அழகைக் கண்டு செருக்கடைந்து இழிவான இன்பத்தை விற்கும் மகளிரின் தோள்களைத் தழுவ மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts two types of people and their values. On one side are those who protect their own moral goodness and reputation. On the other side are public women who proudly use their physical beauty to sell fleeting, base pleasures. The poet states that men who truly value their own virtue will never seek the embrace of such women, as it would destroy their moral standing.

ai.literal: Firm-heart those-without will-embrace in-other-heart feigning those-who-unite's shoulders.
ai.translation: Only men lacking a firm heart will embrace the shoulders of women who unite physically while harboring ulterior motives in their hearts.
ai.modern: மன உறுதி இல்லாதவர்கள் மட்டுமே, உள்ளத்தில் வேறு நோக்கத்தை வைத்துக்கொண்டு உடலால் மட்டும் கூடும் பெண்களின் தோள்களைத் தழுவுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the lack of self-control in men who seek the company of wanton women. The phrase 'piṟa neñcil' (in a different heart) refers to the women's ulterior motive, usually financial gain, which contrasts with their outward show of affection. Only men without 'niṟai neñcam' (a firm, self-controlled mind) will fall for such feigned embraces.

ai.literal: Examining wisdom those-who-are-not-to, a tormenting-spirit they-say, deceitful women's embrace.
ai.translation: They say the embrace of deceitful women is a tormenting spirit to those who lack discerning wisdom.
ai.modern: ஆராய்ந்து அறியும் அறிவு இல்லாதவர்களுக்கு, வஞ்சனை பொருந்திய பெண்களின் தழுவல் ஒரு துன்பம் தரும் அணங்கு என்று கூறுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the false affection of deceitful women who sell their love. It states that their embrace is like being possessed by a tormenting spirit (அணங்கு). Only those who lack the wisdom to examine and understand true intentions fall prey to this illusion. The word 'மாய' highlights the deceptive, illusory nature of their affection, which brings ruin rather than joy.

ai.literal: Bound-without excellent jewel-women's soft shoulders, greatness-without base men sinking hell.
ai.translation: The soft shoulders of excellently jewelled women who know no bounds are a hellish mire into which base men devoid of greatness sink.
ai.modern: எந்த வரைமுறையும் இல்லாத, சிறந்த அணிகலன்களை அணிந்த விலைமகளிரின் மென்மையான தோள்கள், எந்த உயர்வும் இல்லாத கீழ்மக்கள் மூழ்கி அழியும் நரகமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the allure of prostitutes, describing them as women who lack moral boundaries despite their outward beauty and jewels. Their soft shoulders are metaphorically compared to a dangerous swamp or hell. Only base men who lack any true greatness or virtue will allow themselves to sink into such a trap. The word 'அளறு' effectively conveys both a muddy swamp that traps people and the concept of hell.

ai.literal: Double-minded women and, liquor and, gambling and, prosperity to-forsake those-who-experience association.
ai.translation: Double-minded women, liquor, and gambling are the companions of those forsaken by prosperity.
ai.modern: உள்ளத்தில் ஒன்றும் வெளியில் ஒன்றுமாக இருக்கும் விலைமகளிர், கள், சூதாட்டம் ஆகிய மூன்றும் செல்வத்தால் கைவிடப்பட்டவர்களின் தொடர்புகள் ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet groups together three destructive vices: prostitutes, alcohol, and gambling. The phrase 'double-minded women' refers to those who show false affection for money while their true intentions lie elsewhere. The poet states that these three things are the natural companions of people who have been abandoned by prosperity. Indulging in these vices is presented as the defining characteristic of those whose wealth and well-being are completely ruined.
